doc.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Musical tastes at Juilliard: classical, Brubeck and Oscar Peterson
summary: Mainly passionate about classical and opera, with Dave Brubeck and Oscar Peterson as piano models.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I’m wondering what your musical tastes, about the time you went to Juilliard, what music were you passionate about at that time?

Classical I think. I mean I listened to jazz and I was a Dave Brubeck fan at the time, who was — it was on the pop charts at the time. I listed to Dave and I was messing with piano a little bit and trying to play like Dave and copying all his stuff and Oscar Peterson. But mainly I was into classical. I still listen to it a lot. I’m still an opera fan. If I’m in the car it’s usually tuned to a classical station. I think that’s — I’m passionate about all kinds of music if it’s being done well, but I think mostly classical.
